stimuli.text: Initial-rate data for A + B → products:
A student heats 6.2 g of $$\ce{CaCO3(s)}$$, which decomposes completely: $$\ce{CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g)}$$. The $$\ce{CO2}$$ is collected at 312 K and 1.01 atm.
The decomposition of compound X was monitored at constant temperature.
A student titrates 22.0 mL of 0.2 M weak monoprotic acid HA (Ka = 3 \times 10^{-5}) with 0.1 M NaOH.
5.1 g of $$\ce{CaCl2}$$ dissolves in 60 g of water in a coffee-cup calorimeter. The temperature rises by 5.9 °C. Assume the solution's specific heat is 4.18 J/(g·°C).

A galvanic cell is made of a Mg electrode in 1.0 M $$\ce{Mg^{2+}}$$ and a Fe electrode in 1.0 M $$\ce{Fe^{2+}}$$. Standard reduction potentials: $$\ce{Mg^{2+} + 2e- -> Mg}$$ E° = -2.37 V; $$\ce{Fe^{2+} + 2e- -> Fe}$$ E° = -0.44 V.
The photoelectron spectra of Na (Z = 11) and Mg (Z = 12) are compared.

questions.stem: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 39 g. The actual yield is 23 g. What is the percent yield?
What is the pH of a 0.005 M solution of $$\ce{Ba(OH)2}$$ at 25 °C?

options.why: Strong acids and bases ionize completely; no equilibrium is needed.
Each formula unit releases two OH⁻.
Correct. Strong base: [OH⁻] = 2 × 0.005 M; pH = 14 − pOH.
That is the pOH; subtract from 14.

questions.stem: Why is HI a stronger acid than HF?

options.text: F is less electronegative than I
The H–I bond is weaker and I⁻ is larger, so H⁺ is released more easily
options.why: Correct. Bond strength decreases down the group.

questions.explanation: Bond strength decreases down the group.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3}$$, $$\ce{H2}$$ is consumed at 0.18 M/s. At what rate does $$\ce{NH3}$$ form?

options.why: Correct. Multiply by the coefficient ratio 2/3.
Divide by the reactant's coefficient too.

questions.stem: What is the energy of a photon with a wavelength of 385 nm?

options.why: Correct. E = hc/λ, with λ in meters.

questions.stem: Which change alters the value of K?
Samples of $$\ce{Ar}$$, $$\ce{H2}$$, $$\ce{O2}$$, $$\ce{CH4}$$ are all at the same temperature. Which has the highest average molecular speed?

options.why: Ar has a larger molar mass (40 g/mol).
Correct. At the same temperature, average kinetic energy is equal, so the lightest gas moves fastest.
CH4 has a larger molar mass (16 g/mol).
O2 has a larger molar mass (32 g/mol).

questions.explanation: Molar masses: Ar 40, H2 2.02, O2 32, CH4 16.

questions.stem: 49 g of water at 58 °C is mixed with 52 g of water at 25 °C in an insulated container. What is the final temperature?

options.why: Correct. Heat lost = heat gained; for water alone, a mass-weighted average.
Pair each mass with its own temperature.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation number of N in $$\ce{NO2}$$?

options.why: Make the oxidation numbers add up to the overall charge.
Make the oxidation numbers add up to the overall charge.
Make the oxidation numbers add up to the overall charge.
Correct. The oxidation numbers must sum to the species' overall charge (O usually −2, H usually +1).

questions.stem: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?

options.text: It provides a pathway with a lower activation energy
options.why: Correct. The reaction goes by a different mechanism.

questions.explanation: The reaction goes by a different mechanism.

questions.stem: Which substance has the highest boiling point?

options.why: Correct. Water forms extensive hydrogen bonds.

questions.stem: Which compound has the greater lattice energy, $$\ce{BaO}$$ or $$\ce{KBr}$$?

options.text: $$\ce{KBr}$$, because its ions have larger charges
$$\ce{BaO}$$, because its ions have larger charges
options.why: Correct. By Coulomb's law, attraction increases with the product of the ion charges.

options.text: They are equal because both are ionic
$$\ce{KBr}$$, because it has more atoms per formula unit
options.why: Number of atoms does not determine lattice energy.

questions.explanation: BaO has ion charges 2 and 2; KBr has 1 and 1.

questions.stem: How should acetic acid be written in a net ionic equation?

options.why: Correct. It is a weak acid and mostly un-ionized.

options.text: It is always omitted as a spectator

questions.explanation: It is a weak acid and mostly un-ionized.

questions.stem: A weak acid HA has pKa = 7.2. In a solution at pH 6.1, which statement is correct?

options.why: Correct. Below the pKa, the protonated form dominates.

questions.stem: On a reaction energy profile, the reactants are at 51 kJ/mol, the transition state at 91 kJ/mol and the products at 135 kJ/mol. What is the activation energy of the reverse reaction?

options.why: Correct. Reverse Ea = transition state − products.
Measure from the correct starting point.

questions.explanation: Forward Ea = 40, ΔH = 84, reverse Ea = -44 kJ/mol.

questions.stem: Which bond is the most polar?

options.why: Correct. It has the largest electronegativity difference (1.8).

questions.stem: For $$\ce{A(g) + B(g) <=> 2C(g)}$$, K = 7.4. A mixture has [A] = 0.1 M, [B] = 0.9 M and [C] = 0.1 M. In which direction will the reaction proceed?

options.text: It proceeds forward, toward products, because Q = 1.11
It proceeds forward, toward products, because Q = 0.111
options.why: Correct. Q = [C]²/([A][B]) = 0.111, which is less than K.

options.text: It proceeds in reverse, toward reactants, because Q = 0.111
options.why: If Q is less than K, the reaction proceeds forward.

options.text: It is at equilibrium, because Q = K

questions.stem: A gas mixture contains 0.2 mol N₂, 0.7 mol O₂ and 0.4 mol Ar at a total pressure of 3 atm. What is the partial pressure of N₂?

options.why: The gases are not present in equal amounts.
Use the mole fraction, not moles.

questions.stem: On a reaction energy profile, the reactants are at 91 kJ/mol, the transition state at 210 kJ/mol and the products at 39 kJ/mol. What is ΔH for the reaction?

options.why: Measure from the correct starting point.

questions.explanation: Forward Ea = 119, ΔH = -52, reverse Ea = 171 kJ/mol.

questions.stem: Which best explains why the atomic radius of Cl is smaller than that of Na?

options.why: They are in the same period.

options.text: Cl has more protons with similar shielding, so its valence electrons are pulled closer
options.why: Correct. Greater effective nuclear charge across a period.

questions.explanation: Greater effective nuclear charge across a period.

questions.stem: What volume does 0.8 mol of gas occupy at 2.24 atm and 409 K?

options.why: 22.4 L/mol applies only at 0 °C and 1 atm.
Use R = 0.08206 with atm and L.

questions.stem: A gas mixture contains 0.9 mol N₂, 0.5 mol O₂ and 0.8 mol Ar at a total pressure of 4 atm. What is the partial pressure of N₂?

options.why: The gases are not present in equal amounts.
Use the mole fraction, not moles.

questions.stem: Why are metals good conductors of electricity?

options.text: Their valence electrons are delocalized and free to move
Their ions move freely in the solid
options.why: Ions are fixed in the lattice.

questions.stem: A mass spectrum of a sample of copper shows two peaks: mass 63 with relative abundance 58% and mass 65 with 42%. What is the average atomic mass of the sample?

options.why: The isotopes are not equally abundant.
Correct. Weight each isotope mass by its fractional abundance.
Pair each mass with its own abundance.

questions.stem: How many moles are in 24 g of $$\ce{HNO3}$$?

options.why: Correct. n = m/M with M = 63.02 g/mol.

questions.stem: What is the pressure of 0.68 mol of gas in a 10 L container at 337 K?

options.why: With L and atm, use R = 0.08206.

questions.stem: When a salt dissolves in water, the temperature of the solution decreases. Which is true?

options.text: The water's molecules gain kinetic energy
The process is endothermic; energy flows from the water into the dissolving process

questions.stem: In a Zn/Cu galvanic cell, [Zn²⁺] is increased. What happens to the cell potential?

options.why: Correct. A product's concentration rises, so Q increases.

questions.explanation: A product's concentration rises, so Q increases.

questions.stem: A weak acid HA has pKa = 4.9. In a solution at pH 2.5, which statement is correct?

options.why: Correct. Below the pKa, the protonated form dominates.

questions.stem: How many valence electrons are shown in the Lewis structure of $$\ce{HCN}$$?

options.why: Correct. Sum the valence electrons of all atoms, then add one per negative charge (subtract one per positive charge).

questions.stem: What is the pH of a 1 M solution of acetic acid (Ka = 1.8 \times 10^{-5})?

options.why: Correct. Solve Ka = x²/(C − x) for x = [H₃O⁺].
A weak acid does not ionize completely.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{H2(g) + I2(g) <=> 2HI(g)}$$, initial [H₂] = 0.8 M and [I₂] = 0.8 M, with no HI. At equilibrium, [HI] = 1.14 M. What is K?
What is the molecular geometry of $$\ce{HCN}$$?

options.why: Lone pairs change the molecular shape from the electron-domain geometry.
Correct. Count electron domains and lone pairs on the central atom.
Lone pairs change the molecular shape from the electron-domain geometry.
Lone pairs change the molecular shape from the electron-domain geometry.

questions.stem: What is the molarity of a solution made by dissolving 0.199 mol of solute in enough water to make 534 mL of solution?
A 32.7 mL sample of $$\ce{H2SO4}$$ is titrated to the equivalence point with 25.6 mL of 0.165 M NaOH. What is the concentration of the acid?

options.why: Correct. Each H₂SO₄ reacts with two OH⁻, so divide the moles of NaOH by 2.

questions.stem: A first-order reaction has a half-life of 42 min. Starting at 8.7 M, what is the concentration after 210 min?

options.why: Each half-life halves the concentration; it is not divided by 2n.

questions.stem: Which is a physical change?

options.why: Correct. Only intermolecular forces are overcome.

questions.stem: Under which conditions does a real gas deviate most from ideal behavior?

options.why: Correct. Particle volume and attractions matter most.

questions.explanation: Particle volume and attractions matter most.

questions.stem: Samples of $$\ce{N2}$$, $$\ce{Cl2}$$, $$\ce{CH4}$$, $$\ce{Ar}$$ are all at the same temperature. Which has the highest average molecular speed?

options.why: Correct. At the same temperature, average kinetic energy is equal, so the lightest gas moves fastest.
Cl2 has a larger molar mass (70.9 g/mol).
Ar has a larger molar mass (40 g/mol).
N2 has a larger molar mass (28 g/mol).

questions.explanation: Molar masses: N2 28, Cl2 70.9, CH4 16, Ar 40.

questions.stem: What is the molarity of a solution made by dissolving 0.07 mol of solute in enough water to make 338 mL of solution?
At 298 K, ΔG° for a reaction is 6 kJ/mol. What is K?

options.why: Correct. K = e^(−ΔG°/RT), with ΔG° in J/mol and R = 8.314.

questions.explanation: ln K = -2.42; K = 0.0888. Positive ΔG°: K less than 1.

questions.stem: For a reaction, ΔH° = -70 kJ/mol and ΔS° = 221 J/(mol·K). What is ΔG° at 730 K, and is the reaction favorable?

options.why: Convert ΔS from J to kJ.
Correct. ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, with ΔS in kJ/(mol·K).

questions.stem: What is the rate law?

options.why: Correct. Doubling [A] multiplies the rate by 4; doubling [B] multiplies it by 1.
Compare trials where only one concentration changes.
Recheck how the rate changes when [B] doubles.
Orders are found from the data, not from coefficients.

questions.explanation: Trials 1→2: rate ×4, so order 2 in A. Trials 1→3: rate ×1, so order 0 in B.

questions.stem: A solution has an absorbance of 0.202 in a 2 cm cuvette. The molar absorptivity is 84 M⁻¹cm⁻¹. What is the concentration?
A weak acid (pKa 4.74) is titrated with NaOH; the equivalence point is reached at 24.4 mL. What is the pH after 12.2 mL of NaOH has been added?

options.why: That is only for strong acid–strong base equivalence.
Correct. At the half-equivalence point, [HA] = [A⁻], so pH = pKa.

questions.stem: A reaction has K = 8. What is K for the reaction multiplied by 2?

options.why: K is raised to a power, not multiplied.
Correct. Reverse → 1/K; multiply by n → Kⁿ.
Multiplying by n raises K to the nth power.

questions.stem: A compound (glucose) is 40% C, 6.71% H, 53.3% O by mass. What is its empirical formula?

options.why: That is the molecular formula; reduce to the simplest ratio.
Correct. Convert each percent (in 100 g) to moles and divide by the smallest.

questions.explanation: The mole ratio reduces to CH2O; the molecular formula is C6H12O6.

questions.stem: A buffer contains 0.16 mol of a weak acid HA (pKa 3.75) and 0.41 mol of its conjugate base A⁻. Then 0.04 mol of HCl is added. What is the pH?

options.why: Correct. First react: H⁺ converts A⁻ to HA. Then pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]).
Update moles after the added acid or base reacts.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{2Na + Cl2 -> 2NaCl}$$, 90 g of $$\ce{Na}$$ reacts with 88 g of $$\ce{Cl2}$$. What mass of $$\ce{NaCl}$$ can form?

options.why: Correct. Cl2 is the limiting reactant.
Not all of both reactants reacts.
Apply the mole ratio from the equation.
Use the limiting reactant, which gives less product.

questions.stem: The first four ionization energies of an element are 626, 3130, 5196, 9717 kJ/mol. In which group of the periodic table is the element most likely found?

options.why: Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.
Correct. The large jump comes after removing 1 electron, so it has 1 valence electron.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.

questions.explanation: The big jump marks the start of removing core electrons.

questions.stem: For the galvanic cell made from these half-cells, what is ΔG°? (F = 96,485 C/mol)

options.why: ΔG° is negative for a positive E°.
Correct. ΔG° = −nFE° with n = 6 electrons transferred and E° = 1.22 V.

questions.stem: 18 mL of 0.15 M weak acid HA is titrated with 0.09 M NaOH. What volume of NaOH reaches the equivalence point?

options.why: Correct. Moles of base = moles of acid.

questions.stem: A photoelectron spectrum shows 3 peaks. From highest to lowest binding energy, their relative heights are 2 : 2 : 5. Which element is it?

options.why: Correct. The peaks correspond to $$1s^{2}\,2s^{2}\,2p^{5}$$, which has 9 electrons.

questions.stem: The Ksp of $$\ce{Mg(OH)2}$$ is 5.6 \times 10^{-12}. What is its molar solubility in pure water?
Calculate ΔH° for $$\ce{2C2H6 + 7O2 -> 4CO2 + 6H2O(g)}$$. (ΔH°f of O₂ is 0.)

options.why: Correct. Σ n ΔH°f(products) − Σ n ΔH°f(reactants).
Multiply each ΔH°f by its coefficient.

questions.stem: For the galvanic cell made from these half-cells, what is ΔG°? (F = 96,485 C/mol)

options.why: ΔG° is negative for a positive E°.
Correct. ΔG° = −nFE° with n = 2 electrons transferred and E° = 1.93 V.

questions.stem: Reaction 1 has ΔH₁ = -195 kJ and reaction 2 has ΔH₂ = -315 kJ. A target reaction is obtained by doubling reaction 1 and adding reaction 2. What is ΔH for the target reaction?

options.why: Reversing changes the sign of ΔH₂.
Correct. Reverse → change sign; multiply → multiply ΔH; then add.
Enthalpies add; they do not multiply.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{H2(g) + I2(g) <=> 2HI(g)}$$, initial [H₂] = 1.5 M and [I₂] = 1.5 M, with no HI. At equilibrium, [HI] = 2.04 M. What is K?
When a reaction involving 0.067 mol of limiting reactant occurs in 53 g of solution (c = 4.18 J/(g·°C)), the temperature rises by 10.4 °C. What is ΔH for the reaction?

options.why: Correct. q(solution) = mcΔT = 2300 J; q(reaction) = −q(solution); divide by moles.
A temperature rise means the reaction is exothermic (negative ΔH).
Divide by the moles of reactant.

questions.stem: Use the bond enthalpies to estimate ΔH for $$\ce{2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O}$$.

options.why: Broken minus formed, not formed minus broken.
Multiply each bond energy by the number of bonds.
Bonds formed release energy: subtract them.
Correct. ΔH ≈ Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed).

parts.prompt: Calculate the number of moles of CO₂ produced.

rubric.criterion: Correct moles using molar mass 100.09 g/mol and the 1:1 ratio.

parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of CO₂ expected.
The student measures 1.445 L of gas. Calculate the percent yield, and give one experimental reason the yield could be less than 100%.

rubric.example: Incomplete decomposition (not heated long enough) or gas leaking from the apparatus.

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a complete Lewis diagram for CO₂, and identify its molecular geometry and the hybridization of carbon.

rubric.example: O=C=O with two lone pairs on each O (16 valence electrons).

parts.prompt: Explain why CO₂ is nonpolar even though C=O bonds are polar.

rubric.criterion: Linear symmetry makes the bond dipoles cancel.

parts.prompt: CaO is an ionic solid. Explain, using Coulomb's law, why CaO has a higher melting point than KCl.

rubric.criterion: Larger ion charges in CaO (2+/2−) than in KCl (1+/1−).
Greater electrostatic attraction (and smaller ions) means more energy is needed to separate the ions.

parts.prompt: Calculate the average rate of disappearance of X between 0 and 20 s.
Determine the order of the reaction with respect to X. Justify your answer using the data.

rubric.example: Equal time intervals give equal changes in ln[X].

parts.prompt: Write the rate law and determine the rate constant, with units.
Calculate the half-life of the reaction (for the initial concentration).
A proposed mechanism has a slow first step: X → Y + Z. Is the mechanism consistent with the rate law? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Yes; the slow step's elementary rate law matches the observed rate law.

parts.prompt: A catalyst is added. Explain its effect on the rate and on the rate constant, using activation energy.

rubric.example: The catalyst provides a new pathway.

rubric.criterion: Lower activation energy means a larger fraction of collisions are successful.

parts.prompt: Write the net ionic equation for the titration reaction.
Calculate the initial pH of the acid solution.

rubric.criterion: Ka expression set up with x = [H₃O⁺].

parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of NaOH needed to reach the equivalence point.
What is the pH at the half-equivalence point? Justify.
Calculate the pH at the equivalence point.

rubric.criterion: Uses Kb = Kw/Ka and the diluted [A⁻].

parts.prompt: Choose an appropriate indicator from: methyl orange (pKa 3.7), bromothymol blue (pKa 7.0), phenolphthalein (pKa 9.3). Justify.

rubric.criterion: Indicator whose pKa is closest to the equivalence pH.

parts.prompt: Explain why the solution at the half-equivalence point resists pH change when a small amount of HCl is added.

rubric.criterion: A⁻ reacts with added H⁺ to form HA (buffer).
rubric.example: A⁻ + H₃O⁺ → HA + H₂O, so the ratio [A⁻]/[HA] changes only slightly.

parts.prompt: Is the dissolution endothermic or exothermic? Justify.

rubric.example: Exothermic: the solution warmed, so energy was released.

parts.prompt: Calculate the heat absorbed or released by the solution.
Calculate ΔH of dissolution in kJ/mol.
If some heat escaped to the surroundings, would the magnitude of the calculated ΔH be too large or too small? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Too small, because the measured temperature change is smaller than the true change.

parts.prompt: Write the balanced net ionic equation for the cell reaction.
Calculate E°cell.
Calculate ΔG° for the cell reaction.
The concentration of Mg²⁺ is increased to 2.0 M. Predict the effect on the cell potential and justify.

rubric.criterion: E decreases because Q increases (a product's concentration rises).
rubric.example: Q greater than 1 → E less than E°.

questions.title: Solubility of a slightly soluble salt

parts.prompt: Write the Ksp expression.
Calculate the molar solubility in pure water.
Calculate the molar solubility in a solution containing 0.1 M F⁻ (from a soluble salt).
Explain how lowering the pH affects the solubility.

rubric.criterion: Correct reasoning about whether the anion is basic.
rubric.example: Solubility increases: H⁺ reacts with F⁻ (a base), shifting the equilibrium toward dissolving.

parts.prompt: Write the electron configuration of Mg.
Explain why the 1s peak of Mg has a higher binding energy than the 1s peak of Na.

rubric.criterion: Mg has more protons, so 1s electrons are attracted more strongly (Coulomb's law).

parts.prompt: Describe one difference in the number or relative height of peaks between the two spectra.

rubric.criterion: A valid difference based on configurations.
rubric.example: Mg has one more electron, so its outermost peak is taller or an extra peak appears.

parts.prompt: Which element has the larger atomic radius? Justify using Coulomb's law.

rubric.criterion: Na: fewer protons with similar shielding, so valence electrons are held less tightly.
rubric.example: Same period; effective nuclear charge increases across.
